name: Reveri (self-hypnosis app)
founders: David Spiegel, MD (Stanford psychiatry; co-founder, scientific advisor / Chief Scientific Officer)
founded_year_range: 2017-2020: the Stanford pilot of an Alexa/app automated self-hypnosis program (NCT03931772) started Sept 2017; press dates the company (Reveri Health, Inc.) to 2020; iOS app first released 9 Mar 2021; the site gives no founding year
cost_summary: US prices, verified Oct 2026: $149.99/yr, $44.95/mo, or $449 lifetime. 7-day free trial; 7-day refund window; free hardship memberships via 'Reveri for Good'.
mechanisms: autonomic/nervous system dysregulation (sympathetic overdrive, "stuck in fight-or-flight")
hypnotic focused attention, dissociation and suggestibility (trait hypnotizability)
mechanism_summary: Hypnosis is framed as a distinct brain state of focused attention, dissociation and suggestibility. It reduces dACC/salience ('alarm') activity, increases DLPFC-insula coupling and decreases DLPFC-DMN coupling (Jiang et al. 2017), which allows top-down modulation of pain and stress and lowers arousal. Trait hypnotizability, screened in-app with a remote Hypnotic Induction Profile, predicts benefit. There is no disease-specific theory of chronic illness: symptoms are treated as states that attention and suggestion can modulate.
roots: Spiegel Hypnotic Induction Profile (Herbert & David Spiegel)
techniques: eye-roll/eye-closure induction with slow breath and floating sensation
mainstream_notes: The app is a direct-to-consumer wellness subscription with no FDA clearance; no payer, health-system or guideline adoption was found. The underlying clinical hypnosis (Spiegel's method, used at Stanford) and hypnosis generally have mainstream footing, e.g. guideline-endorsed gut-directed hypnotherapy for IBS and procedural analgesia.
insurance_notes: The app is self-pay. Clinician-delivered hypnosis within psychotherapy can sometimes be billed, but that is not Reveri.

key_trials.citation: Tran N, Saperia C, Neri E, Jo B, Kim B, Zewde N, Nouriani B, Kinderman C, Jagielo A, Faerman A, Maldonado J, Spiegel D. Effects of app delivered self hypnosis on stress management. npj Digit Med 2025; PMID 41413254
key_trials.design: Retrospective uncontrolled analysis of in-app pre/post ratings (282,893 sessions), Nov 2021-Jan 2025; co-founder author
key_trials.finding: Single-item stress fell about 1.5/10 per session (d about 0.71-0.78) across the first 10 sessions; no cumulative improvement; larger effects with interactive and regular-length sessions, higher hypnotizability, older age and paying members

key_trials.citation: Saperia C, Bharti S, Kim B, Jo B, Neri E, Markovits J, Nouriani B, Kinderman C, Tran N, Maldonado J, Lev-Ari S, Spiegel D. Effect of app based hypnosis on pain reduction in a large user cohort. Research Square preprint, posted 9 Sep 2026 (not peer reviewed)
key_trials.design: Retrospective uncontrolled real-world pre/post cohort of 'Manage Pain' module users (59,147 sessions), Dec 2021-Jul 2025
key_trials.finding: Pain fell 1.16-1.3/10 per session (ES about 0.53-0.62); in session 1, 22.5% had >50% reduction, 18.7% had no change and 6.6% got worse; no cumulative change

key_trials.citation: Caggiano L, Karayannis NV, Collins C, Grooms D, Simon JE. A Brief Hypnosis Intervention Improves Single-Limb Dynamic Balance in People with Chronic Ankle Instability: A Crossover Experimental Pilot Study. Int J Clin Exp Hypn 2025;73(2):181-197; PMID 40020194; NCT06390072 (independent, Ohio University; used the Reveri track 'Hypnosis Prep for Workout')
key_trials.design: Randomized crossover pilot: 8-min Reveri self-hypnosis track vs 8-min ankle-education video; unblinded; single session
key_trials.finding: Modest improvement in lateral dynamic balance only; no pain or symptom outcome

key_trials.citation: Stanford University (PI Spiegel D). Online Automated Self-Hypnosis Program. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03931772 (2017-2022)
key_trials.design: Non-randomized single-group open pilot (smoking-cessation and pain arms) via Amazon Alexa or the Reveri app
key_trials.finding: Completed Feb 2022; no results posted and no publication found

key_trials.citation: Lang EV, Benotsch EG, Fick LJ, ... Spiegel D. Adjunctive non-pharmacological analgesia for invasive medical procedures: a randomised trial. Lancet 2000;355:1486-90 (generic in-person hypnosis, not the app)
key_trials.design: RCT: self-hypnotic relaxation vs structured attention vs standard care
key_trials.finding: Pain stayed flat with hypnosis (it rose with standard care), with less drug use and shorter procedures

controversy: The app is marketed with 'science settled' rhetoric, but there is no RCT of the app for a chronic symptom; the only randomized use is a single-session ankle-balance pilot (N = 24). Its evidence is founder-co-authored, uncontrolled single-item pre/post data, and an early Stanford pilot (NCT03931772) is unpublished. Pain claims borrow from generic hypnosis trials, and the '77% feel better' figure is unsourced. An RCT of a different hypnosis app (Lang 2021, IJCEH) found only modest advantages over a control app. Amplification came through celebrity podcasts (Huberman, Ferriss). The monthly price is high, and benefit is limited for low-hypnotizable users. It makes no cure claims for ME/CFS-type illnesses and carries wellness disclaimers.

popularity.reach_estimate: About 300k-1M cumulative registered users. Press reported more than 300k registered users by Aug 2023; at least 84k used the stress module and at least 19k the pain module through 2025. Google Play shows 100K+ downloads and iOS 4,487 ratings (Oct 2026). A claim of more than 1.2M installs from search snippets is not on the live careers page.
popularity.method_notes: Based on user and session counts in the peer-reviewed npj paper and the preprint, the 2023 press figure of more than 300k registered users, the Huberman episode date (the main amplification event, 21 Feb 2022), the 2023 UK rebrand and quit-vaping content, and the AI relaunch and publications in 2025-26. 2017-2019 reflects the Stanford Alexa pilot. App-store figures were checked Oct 2026 (iOS first released 9 Mar 2021). Reddit (automated access blocked) and Google Trends (no programmatic access) could not be checked; the trajectory is coarse and inferred.
